column1: # TITLE: Response to a LNA miR-92a inhibitor in immortalized human bronchial epithelial cells.
# SUMMARY: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related fatalities. Recent success developing genotypically-targeted therapies
column2: with potency only in well-defined subpopulations of tumors
column3: suggests a path to improving patient survival. We utilized a library of oligonucleotide inhibitors to microRNAs
column4: a class of post-transcriptional gene regulators
column5: to identify novel synthetic lethal interactions between miRNA inhibition and molecular mechanisms in NSCLC. Two inhibitors
column7: produced a toxicity distribution across a panel of 27 cell lines that correlated with loss of p53 protein expression. Notably
column8: depletion of p53 was sufficient to confer sensitivity to otherwise resistant telomerase-immortalized bronchial epithelial cells. We found that both miR inhibitors cause sequence-specific down-regulation of the miR-17~92 polycistron
column9: and this down-regulation was toxic only in the context of p53 loss. Mechanistic studies indicated the selective toxicity of miR-17~92 polycistron inactivation was the consequence of derepression of vitamin D signaling via suppression of CYP24A1; a rate limiting enzyme in the 1α
column11: high CYP24A1 expression significantly correlated with poor patient outcome in multiple lung cancer cohorts. Our results indicate that the screening approach utilized in this study can identify clinically relevant synthetic lethal interactions
column12: and that vitamin D receptor agonists may show enhanced efficacy in p53-negative lung cancer patients.
